$comment: The web <-> native bridge, protocol 1 (docs/NATIVE_APP_SPEC.md). Read by packages/native tests and native/ios tests: change both together.

origins.any: Any page of ours (the portal or an app), main frame only.
origins.app: Only an app's page whose GET /native/config entry lists the call's `capability` (its manifest's `native`). The portal may not.

events.doc: Streams (motion) arrive as window.stacksNative._emit(channel, payload); pages subscribe with window.stacksNative.listen(channel, fn), which returns a function that unsubscribes. A batch holds every sample since the last frame. Units: g (acceleration, gravity), rad/s (rotationRate), rad (attitude); `t` is seconds since the stream started.

app.info.doc: The app's version, build, the git commit CI built it from ("" for a local Xcode build; absent in builds made before this field), and platform.

auth.apple.doc: Native Sign in with Apple. The identity token is addressed to the app's bundle ID; `name` is what Apple shared (only on the first sign-in, else ""). Only the portal's own page may ask.

auth.google.doc: Native Google sign-in. The ID token is addressed to the web client (serverClientID). Only the portal's own page may ask.

auth.signedOut.doc: The person signed out everywhere: the app forgets its Google session and this device's push registration, and clears the badge.

badge.set.doc: Sets the app icon's number (unread notifications plus requests waiting), so it's right while the app is open.

camera.locate.doc: Finds `codes` (QR payloads, e.g. on a big screen) with the back camera and says which way each is from the phone. The app shows its own camera view (with `prompt` and Cancel; the page never sees a frame) and answers once every code has stayed steady for `holdMs` (300-5000, default 1500), or fails with `failed` after `timeoutMs` (2000-30000, default 10000). `cancelled`: Cancel; `forbidden`: camera access is off. Each code's `centre` and four `corners` are unit vectors in the phone's frame (CoreMotion axes: x right edge, y top edge, z out of the screen; the back camera looks along -z), and `attitude` is the motion stream's at that moment, so they combine with its samples. Needs a running motion stream (`motion.start`). Apps that declare "camera" (sensitive).

haptics.impact.doc: A tap you feel (UIImpactFeedbackGenerator). Apps that declare "haptics".

haptics.notification.doc: A success, warning or error buzz (UINotificationFeedbackGenerator).

haptics.pattern.doc: A custom pattern (Core Haptics): at most 32 events within 5 s. `t` and `duration` in seconds; `intensity` and `sharpness` 0-1; an event with `duration` is continuous, else a tap.

motion.start.doc: Streams CoreMotion device motion at `hz` (10-100; asked-for rates are clamped) to `channel`, batched once per display frame (see events). `sensors` picks the fields of each sample (default all four). Starting again stops the previous stream. Stops when the page goes away; pauses while the app is in the background. Apps that declare "motion".

motion.stop.doc: Stops the stream on `channel` (no error if it already stopped).

push.register.doc: Asks for permission (the system prompt, the first time) and returns the APNs token for the portal to register with POST /devices. `cancelled` when the person says no; `env` is sandbox for Xcode builds.

push.saveDevice.doc: Keeps the platform's device id and secret in the Keychain (the secret answers lock-screen actions, N3b).

push.status.doc: Whether this device may show notifications, and the device id the platform gave it (null until registered).

screen.immersive.doc: `on`: hides the status bar and home indicator and turns off swipe-back and pull-to-refresh, until turned off or the page goes away.

screen.keepAwake.doc: `on`: the screen doesn't dim or lock, until turned off or the page goes away.

screen.lockOrientation.doc: Locks to `portrait` or `landscape`; `any` unlocks. Unlocked when the page goes away.

share.page.doc: What the app's own Share button (bottom right) shares on this page. `page` is location.href when the page set it: the setting applies only while the main frame is on that URL and lapses when it changes or a new document loads. `url` (https only) and `title` default to the page's own; `hidden` takes the button away on that page. Send it again with only `page` to go back to the default.
